extracted.intended_audience: hospital finance officers, Medicare cost report preparers, GME administrators, and hospital compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Medicare/ICD regulatory guidance on (1) redistribution of residency slots after teaching hospital closures, (2) Medicare nursing and allied health (NAH) education pass-through payments and Medicare+Advantage (MA) adjustments, and (3) cost-reporting procedures (Worksheet A, A-8, B-1, B-2) including order-of-operations for offsetting tuition and allocating overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB ratio cap and rolling average calculation for merged hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first two cost reporting periods following a merger, the rolling average must be calculated as though the hospitals had been merged for the entirety of their prior- and penultimate-year cost reporting periods; prior-year and denominator components are the combined values from each hospital's applicable cost reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure applies whether the merger occurs mid-cost-reporting-period or at the start of a new period. Example provided: prior-year numerator = sum of hospitals' IME FTE counts (per Worksheet E, Part A instructions); prior-year denominator = combined available bed count; IRB ratio cap = combined prior-year numerator ÷ combined beds. Beginning with later specified cost reports, normal (post‑transition) calculations apply. See the direct GME example earlier in the preamble for rolling-average demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5506 redistribution process and application timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: When a teaching hospital that trained residents closes, CMS will notify the public and initiate an application/selection round under section 5506 of the ACA to redistribute FTE resident slots to qualifying hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application period is 90 days following notice of closure. Applications must be submitted electronically using Medicare Electronic Application Request Information System (MEARIS™); applications submitted by any other method will not be considered. CMS provides resources and technical support links within MEARIS; application-related questions may be submitted via MEARIS 'Contact'. CMS has not established a deadline by which final determinations will be issued but will review all timely applications and notify applicants as soon as possible. Applicants should consult the CMS DGME website for additional section 5506 policy and procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved NAH education program eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Under existing regulations at 42 CFR 413.85, an 'approved nursing and allied health education program' is a planned program of study that is licensed by State law, or if licensing is not required, accredited by a recognized national professional organization, and must be operated by a provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory history and examples of accrediting bodies were previously listed (e.g., Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs), but the rule reiterates the general licensure-or-accreditation requirement and the provider-operation requirement for NAH pass-through payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unlawful discrimination by NAH programs and accreditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that individual NAH education programs and NAH accrediting bodies must not discriminate, or promote or encourage discrimination, on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or religion, including use of those characteristics or intentional proxies as selection criteria for employment, program participation, resource allocation, or similar activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy would be effective October 1, 2026 and codified under proposed new 42 CFR 413.84, cross-referenced by §413.85 as necessary. This mirrors a similar policy finalized previously for approved medical residency program accreditation criteria in the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of enumerated accreditor list from §413.85(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove from §413.85(e) the language specifying individual accrediting organizations and instead retain the general requirement that an approved NAH program be licensed or accredited by the recognized national professional organization for the activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: listing a limited number of accreditors is no longer useful given the evolving field and many accrediting bodies; rulemaking will keep the general standard and remove specific named examples from regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAH Medicare+Advantage (MA) payment pool calculation and hospital share formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The hospital's NAH MA payment is computed by applying a ratio that accounts for hospital-specific NAH Part A payments, total inpatient days, and MA inpatient days to national totals of the same variables from cost reporting periods ending in the fiscal year two years prior to the current calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formula (as stated): (((Hospital NAH pass-through payment/Hospital Part A Inpatient Days) * (Hospital MA Inpatient Days)) ÷ ((National NAH pass-through payment/National Part A Inpatient Days) * (National MA Inpatient Days))) * Current Year Payment Pool. The Secretary has discretion to 'estimate' national components. CMS uses HCRIS data from the fiscal year two years prior (e.g., FY 2023 HCRIS for CY 2025) and projects current-year payments using the increases allowed by section 1886(h) and CPI-U; rates and percent reductions are published annually in IPPS proposed and final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of HCRIS data and projection methodology for national amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses the best available cost reporting data from HCRIS for the fiscal year two years prior to the current calendar year to determine national NAH pass-through payments, Part A inpatient days, and MA inpatient days, and then projects current-year payments using statutory increases and CPI-U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the FY 2027 proposed rule, CMS proposed to use FY 2023 HCRIS (third quarterly HCRIS update of 2025) to compile national amounts for CY 2025 and intends to update numbers in the final rule based on latest cost report data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of operations for determining net cost of approved NAH educational activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulatory change to 42 CFR 413.85(d)(2)(i) and (ii): net cost is determined by taking allowable direct costs incurred by the provider for trainee stipends and compensation of faculty employed by the provider and subtracting from those direct costs the revenues the provider receives from students (e.g., tuition, student fees, textbooks) prior to allocating indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After subtracting revenues from allowable direct costs, indirect costs would then be allocated to the NAH cost centers (limited to costs the provider itself incurs in connection with operation of its approved educational activities), consistent with Medicare cost-finding principles at 42 CFR 413.24. Effective date proposed for cost reporting periods beginning on or after October 1, 2026. The proposal does not change the existing exclusion that net NAH costs do not include patient care costs, costs incurred by related organizations, redistributions from educational institutions, or community support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to avoid understating Administrative & General (A&G) allocation when NAH revenue offsets exceed direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If tuition and other revenues exceed direct NAH program costs (producing a zero or negative balance on Worksheet A after offset), providers may take steps to ensure A&G allocation is not understated for NAH cost centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed procedure: (1) providers offset the total revenue generated by each NAH program producing a credit (negative) balance on Worksheet A; (2) providers use the reconciliation column on Worksheet B-1 to adjust the accumulated cost statistic by the total amount of NAH revenue offset on Worksheet A-8—effectively reversing that offset for overhead allocation only (in cost report software, indicate 'override with value' and add this value to existing accumulated cost); (3) stepdown on Worksheet B, Part I continues normally. Example provided with numeric illustration (Hospital A: $1,000,000 direct costs, $1,200,000 tuition → ($200,000) on Worksheet A; add $1,200,000 in B-1 reconciliation).

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS offers MAC permission and statistical-basis flexibilities for allocating A&G
rubrics_metrics.description: To mitigate reductions in allocated overhead that may result from deducting revenue prior to overhead allocation, a provider may seek permission from its Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) to utilize a statistical basis other than accumulated cost for allocating indirect costs to NAH cost centers, and may componentize its Administrative & General (line 5) cost center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explained that providers may elect to subscript their A&G cost center for overhead costs directly related to NAH programs and use a statistical basis that accurately reflects services rendered to those departments. This is intended to prevent inappropriate reductions in overhead allocation when revenue offsets create credit balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of allowable indirect costs for NAH pass-through payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs allocated to NAH cost centers are limited to those costs that the provider itself incurs in connection with the operation of its approved educational activities, consistent with Medicare cost-finding principles at 42 CFR 413.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS clarifies that net NAH costs do not include patient care costs, costs incurred by a related organization, redistributions from educational institutions to a provider, or costs provided through community support. The proposed regulatory text preserves these exclusions and refines the treatment of allowable indirect costs and associated cost-reporting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-report worksheet instructions and Transmittal 12 clarifications (order-of-operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmittal 12 clarified that revenue adjustments for NAH programs (tuition, fees, books) should be entered on Worksheet A-8 (line 19) and not applied as post-stepdown adjustments on Worksheet B-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worksheet roles: Worksheet A lines 20 and 23 capture direct costs for nursing and allied health programs; Worksheet A-6 reclassifies costs between cost centers; Worksheet A-8 adjusts expenses including revenue offsets (entered on line 19); Worksheets B, Part I and B-1 accommodate the stepdown allocation of indirect costs; Worksheet B-2 is for post-stepdown adjustments but should not be used to reduce NAH total allowable costs by tuition/fees per Transmittal 12. CMS proposed regulatory changes to align §413.85(d)(2)(i) with Transmittal 12 and provided added technical context to show consistency with Medicare cost-finding principles.
